6	# Hall Use and Conduct Rules
7	Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

9	## 1. Responsibility
10	1.1 These rules were adopted on 12 February 2025.
11	1.2 The named hirer is responsible for guests and suppliers.
12	1.3 Hirers must remain on site throughout their events.
13	1.4 Hirers must follow the safety rules in hall-safety.md.
14	
15	## 2. Behaviour
16	2.1 Threatening or abusive behaviour is not permitted.
17	2.2 Smoking and vaping are prohibited inside the building.
18	2.3 Illegal activities are prohibited anywhere on hall grounds.
19	2.4 Animals are not permitted except assistance animals.
20	2.5 Decorations must not be attached with nails or screws.
21	
22	## 3. Alcohol
23	3.1 Alcohol may be served only with prior written permission.
24	3.2 Alcohol may not be sold under an ordinary hall booking.
25	3.3 Permission to serve alcohol requires the damage deposit in hall-fees.md.
26	3.4 The hirer must ensure alcohol is not supplied to underage guests.
27	3.5 Alcohol must not be taken outside the designated hall grounds.
28	
29	## 4. Music and noise
30	4.1 Amplified music must stop by 22:00 on Friday and Saturday.
31	4.2 Amplified music must stop by 21:00 on all other days.
32	4.3 External speakers are not permitted.
33	4.4 Doors and windows must remain closed during amplified music.
34	4.5 The booking officer may require immediate noise reduction.
35	
36	## 5. Cleaning and damage
37	5.1 Hirers must leave rooms clean and furniture in its original layout.
38	5.2 All rubbish must be placed in the designated outdoor bins.
39	5.3 Kitchen surfaces must be wiped after use.
40	5.4 Damage must be reported within 24 hours after the event.
41	5.5 Reasonable repair costs may be deducted under hall-refunds.md.
42

44	6.1 Serious breaches may result in immediate termination of the event.

# Booking Desk Quick Guide
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Using this guide
This sheet was last refreshed on 10 July 2026.
It is a convenience summary, not a governing document.
The governing documents and hall-changes.md always prevail.
Check the event and cancellation dates before quoting a price.

## 2. Rooms and prices
The Main Hall normally costs £28 an hour.
The Meeting Room costs £12 an hour.
The kitchen costs another £8 per booking.
Bookings normally last at least two hours per room.
Registered village groups generally get 25% off room hire.
Projectors cost £15 and portable speakers cost £10.
Display boards cost £5 per set.
Equipment and kitchen charges do not receive the group discount.

## 3. Booking and payment
Bookings can be requested up to a year ahead.
Allow at least three days before the event.
A booking is not accepted until confirmed in writing.
A £30 booking deposit is normally required.
The outstanding hire bill is generally due two weeks before the event.
Alcohol events also need a £100 damage deposit.

## 4. Opening and attendance
Monday to Thursday events now finish by 21:30.
Friday and Saturday events may run until 23:00.
Sunday events finish by 21:00.
The Main Hall holds up to 90 people.
The Meeting Room holds up to 24 people.
Combined events are limited to 100 people in the building.

## 5. Music and cancellations
Friday and Saturday amplified music stops at 21:30.
Music stops by 21:00 on other days.
Early cancellation may qualify for a full or partial refund.
Mid-range cancellations now generally receive 25% rather than 50%.
The booking deposit is normally kept when a hirer cancels.

## 6. Questions to refer
Check hall-refunds.md before promising any repayment.
Refer safety issues immediately to a trustee.
Do not settle disputed damage charges at the booking desk.

content.text:
**Attendance: within the limit.**
- The Meeting Room holds a maximum of 24 people, and that count includes organisers and children (hall-bookings.md 4.2, 4.4).
- 16 children plus 5 adults is 21, which is under 24.
- The hirer must count attendees when the event begins (hall-safety.md 3.2).
- 19 October 2025 is a Sunday, so the hall's hours are 09:00 to 21:00 and guests must leave by closing (hall-bookings.md 3.3, 3.4). The changes register has no entry that alters this for that date.

**Leaving the children unsupervised: not permitted.**
- Children under 12 must remain under adult supervision (hall-safety.md 3.3). All the children are aged 8 to 11, so the rule covers them all.
- The rules make no exception for preparing another room, and setup must happen within booked hours (hall-bookings.md 3.5).
- At least one responsible adult must also remain near the main entrance (hall-safety.md 3.4).
- The hirer must stay on site throughout the event (hall-conduct.md 1.3).

**What the rules don't say.**
- They don't define "supervision" and set no adult-to-child ratio.
- They don't say whether some adults may prepare another room while others stay with the children.
- The rules therefore don't forbid that arrangement outright. They require only that the children stay under adult supervision at all times, and that an adult remains near the main entrance. Whether a particular arrangement counts as adequate supervision isn't something I can determine from these documents.
- The documents don't cover the other room, such as whether it needs its own booking. Any attendance in it would also count toward the building-wide limit of 100 (hall-bookings.md 4.3).
